items.title: Alphonse Picou Interview, 1958-04-04
items.q: Because I think Barney Bigard now changed and uses his double, what they call a double embouchure.

ctx.x: All of them. Are there some habits that are harder to break than others? Oh, yeah. I mean, what is it that you have to break them up you usually find?

No, they've got... They've got some people, if you can take a try of that, and they blow there, and they blow so nicely. How do you like that? The other ones can't blow nothing. Do you remember the TOs or any other players here that if they were the old-time clarinetists, did they ever cover both the teeth, the upper teeth too? No. Only the bottom. Only the bottom. The TOs didn't cover both. Only the bottom. Because I think Barney Bigard now changed and uses his double, what they call a double embouchure. Oh,…

How long have you spent sometimes with one pupil? I mean, have you worked with one boy over many years? Or is it just a matter of months? How long does it usually take for you to teach somebody? Well... What's the longest you ever took?
